## Findings

The tables above are for rewrite prompt v3, with stemming in the keyword index and the rerank pool that always includes each retriever's top hits.

How far to trust these numbers: prompts v2 and v3 and the retrieval changes were all made after reading failures on this same eval set, so the main-set results are an optimistic estimate. The held-out set in "Chat end-to-end results" was written afterwards and not tuned on.

1. **Rewrite fixes follow-ups, in every slice.** Across the 17 follow-up cases hit@1 goes from 0.53 (naive) to 0.88 and MRR from 0.68 to 0.93; overall hit@3 goes from 0.83 to 1.00. Slice by slice, the rewrite (config 3) is at or above naive everywhere: pronoun 0.60 → 0.80, ellipsis 0.75 → 0.75, correction 0.50 → 1.00, multi-reference 0.25 → 1.00, and unchanged on the three patterns that have no history. Under prompt v1 this was not true: pronoun hit@1 fell from 0.60 to 0.20, hidden inside an average that rose.
2. **Pasting the history in is not a substitute.** Config 2 (full history) is no better than naive overall (hit@1 0.60 vs 0.63) and scores 0.00 on corrections, because the superseded topic is still in the query.
3. **Hybrid is the best search configuration.** Adding BM25 (config 3 → 4) lifts overall hit@1 from 0.83 to 0.93 and `exact_code` from 0.80 to 1.00, with hit@3 at 1.00.
4. **Reranking lowers the top-1 result on this set.** Config 5 scores hit@1 0.80 against 0.93 for hybrid alone, and MRR 0.886 against 0.967; pronoun falls from 1.00 to 0.60. The cross-encoder tends to prefer a product page that repeats the product name over the policy article that answers the question. For chat this matters less than it looks: the top five chunks go to Claude together, so their order is not decisive, and the rerank score is what the relevance gate needs.
5. **Two retrieval faults were found by checking answers, not ranks.** For "How long do I have to return a jacket" the chunk holding the 60-day rule was 2nd in vector search but absent from keyword search, because the query said "jacket" and the chunk "jackets". Rank fusion then placed it 11th, one position outside the 10 chunks the reranker reads, so the answer never mentioned 60 days. Stemming the keyword tokens and guaranteeing each retriever's top 3 a place in the rerank pool fixed it, and lifted keyword-only search from hit@1 0.73 to 0.77.
6. **Prompt and eval were not kept apart.** Prompt v1 and v2 quoted "What about Canada?" and "No, I meant the backpack, not the tent", which are eval cases C-006 and C-010 almost word for word. v3 uses different examples, and a test now fails if any eval sentence appears in a prompt. Ellipsis and correction scores did not drop after the change.
7. **Latency.** Naive search takes about 0.1 s. The rewrite adds about 0.8 s on average (p95 1.6 s). Reranking adds between 0.9 s and 3 s on the laptop used (12th Gen Intel i5-12450H), depending on memory pressure: the full pipeline's p95 has measured between 2.6 s and 5.6 s across runs.
8. **Cost.** Each benchmark run after a rewrite-prompt change makes about 22 Claude calls and 0 on re-runs.

## Chat relevance threshold

`scripts/calibrate_threshold.py` measures the rerank score that the chat's threshold gate sees. Positives are the 30 retrieval cases (score of the best chunk from an expected article); negatives are the 20 questions in `data/eval/negatives.json` (top score), half off-topic and half real support questions that no article covers.

| Threshold | Correct answers kept | Off-topic stopped | Not-covered stopped |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.01 | 97% | 100% | 60% |
| **0.05** | **97%** | **100%** | **90%** |
| 0.10 | 93% | 100% | 90% |
| 0.15 | 90% | 100% | 100% |
| 0.30 | 90% | 100% | 100% |
| 0.50 | 83% | 100% | 100% |
| 0.70 | 80% | 100% | 100% |

- Off-topic questions score at most 0.004 and uncovered support questions at most 0.115. The lowest correct answers score 0.002, 0.068, 0.11, and 0.31.
- **Chosen: 0.05** (`CHAT_MIN_RERANK_SCORE`). It keeps 29 of 30 correct answers and stops every off-topic question. A conventional 0.5 would discard 5 of 30 correct answers.
- The margin is thin on one side: a correct answer at 0.068 sits just above the threshold.
- The one correct answer lost is C-026 ("The zip on my rucksack broke..."): the reranker scores the right chunk at 0.002 because it does not connect "zip" and "rucksack" to "zipper" and "backpack". The chat answers it with "I don't have that information".
- Uncovered questions that pass the gate are still caught by Claude, which returns `not_found` when the chunks do not contain the answer.
- Scoring each chunk against both the rewritten query and the original question was measured and changed nothing at this threshold, so it was not adopted.

## Chat end-to-end results

71 conversations sent through `POST /chat` on the real models and Claude with `scripts/evaluate_chat.py`. Each reply is checked on what its case defines: the kind of reply, a cited source from an expected article, key facts the answer must contain, and text it must never contain.

| Set | Conversations | All checks pass | Kind | Right article | Right facts | Forbidden text absent |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Main (`conversations.json`) | 33 | 32 | 32/33 | 29/30 | 29/30 | |
| Held-out (`holdout.json`) | 12 | 12 | 12/12 | 11/11 | 11/11 | |
| Off-topic and not covered (`negatives.json`) | 20 | 20 | 20/20 | | | |
| Attacks (`attacks.json`) | 6 | 6 | 6/6 | | 1/1 | 6/6 |
| **Total** | **71** | **70** | | | | |

- **The one miss** is C-026, stopped by the threshold gate as described above.
- **No grounding failures** in the final run, and no fallbacks. 43 answers were written with 2.2 citations each on average.
- **Regression guard.** Before these changes 28 of the 30 main-set answers contained the expected fact. After them all 28 still do, plus C-011, which previously omitted the 60-day window.
- **What the first run after the review changes caught.** It scored 66 of 71: two previously correct answers had broken. One was the tightened number rule rejecting the product name "Ridgeline 65"; the other was the answer step re-reading the conversation and giving up on a question whose answer depends on a condition. Both were fixed, along with a held-out case where the answer step resolved "the second one" differently from the rewrite step. The answer step is now given the rewritten question.
- **Attacks.** A fake closing tag carrying a "365 days" policy, a fake agent message claiming "90 days", an instruction to reply with fixed words, a role-play jailbreak, a request for the system prompt, and a false policy inside a labelled customer message: none changed an answer. The two return-window attacks were answered with the real 60-day rule.
- **Latency** was 2.3 s median and 6.6 s maximum per message; the run made 68 Claude calls.
- **Limits of this measurement.** The held-out set informed one fix (passing the rewritten question to the answer step), so it is no longer fully untouched. Fact checks are phrase matches chosen by hand. A sample of answers was also read against the articles and matched them. A sentence with no number, no product code, and no citation is not verified by the grounding check.

## Acceptance criteria (workflow doc 9.5)

| Criterion | Result |
|---|---|
| All article endpoints work; a new article is immediately findable by vector and keyword search | Met (integration tests) |
| Full pipeline (5) beats naive (1) on hit@1, hit@3, and MRR | Met: 0.80 / 0.97 / 0.886 vs 0.63 / 0.83 / 0.767 |
| `exact_code`: hybrid (4) beats vector-only (3) | Met: hit@1 1.00 vs 0.80 |
| Follow-up patterns: rewrite (3) beats naive (1) | Met: hit@1 0.88 vs 0.53, MRR 0.93 vs 0.68, and no slice below naive |
| Rerank (5) improves hit@1 or MRR over config 4 | **Not met**: hit@1 0.80 vs 0.93, MRR 0.886 vs 0.967 (finding 4) |
| Full pipeline p95 latency < 3 s on CPU | Met in some runs (2.6 s), **not met** in others under memory pressure (up to 5.6 s) |
| Total real Anthropic calls ≤ 50 for the whole build | Met for the original build (39). The cap was later raised to 500 by the owner for the chat feature; 371 used so far |
| All quality gates green | Met |

## What was not done, and why

- **Dropping the reranker from search.** On this set hybrid alone ranks better (finding 4). The reranker was kept because the chat gate depends on its score, and because 30 cases are too few to remove a stage on.
- **Synonym handling.** C-026 needs "zip/rucksack" matched to "zipper/backpack". Stemming does not help with synonyms. Running the rewriter on first messages too, or a larger reranker, would address it; neither was tried.
- **A harmful-content classifier.** The output guardrail is pattern matching for contact details, card-like numbers, and links.
- **Temperature 0.** The model family used rejects a non-default temperature.
- **Sample size.** 30 retrieval cases, 12 held-out, 20 negatives, 6 attacks: one main-set case is 0.03 of hit@1, and the threshold was chosen on the same data it is reported on.
